subject: Lighthouse Health MAP: evaluation evidence needs, acceptance tests, and close triggers
messages:
From: Laura Benton <laura.benton@lighthousehealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation window + acceptance criteria (MAP kickoff)

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — our clinical ops and platform leads were impressed with the latency profile and the KV caching demo. We have a 6-week evaluation window budgeted and need to lock down a mutual action plan (MAP) that covers:
- Concrete acceptance tests (functional + non-functional) we can run in our environment
- Evidence artifacts we need to collect for procurement and security
- A go/no-go decision date so procurement can prepare POs if we pass
Can you send a draft MAP and a short checklist of acceptance tests we should run (we care about inference tail-latency, cost per 1k tokens, and PII handling in requests)? Samir (cc) will coordinate SOC2 evidence requests.

Thanks,
Laura Benton
Chief Product Officer
Lighthouse Health

Attachments: Lighthouse_MAP_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Laura Benton <laura.benton@lighthousehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation window + acceptance criteria (MAP kickoff)

Laura — great to kick this off. Draft plan attached (MAP_v1.pdf). High level proposal below so your team can react quickly:

Proposal highlights (draft):
- Evaluation window: 6 weeks (start: 2026-07-20, decision: 2026-08-31)
- Exit gates: pass all critical acceptance tests OR one compensating control + documented risk acceptance
- Acceptance tests (examples we propose):
  * Functional: accuracy/concordance on 200 curated clinical prompts (target F1 > 0.82 on named entity match)
  * Latency: 95th percentile < 280ms for 512-token responses under your expected concurrency profile
  * Cost: measured token cost per 1k under the proposed batching config and target < $3.50 per 1k tokens (post-quantization)
  * Security: no sensitive PHI persisted in logs; pass the SOC2 evidence checklist items we flagged
- Evidence artifacts you should collect: sample logs (anonymized), perf traces, small sample of model outputs with ground truth annotations, and the runbook we provide for KV cache warming
- Roles & owners: we listed internal owners in the attached MAP (technical owner: Karthik; commercial owner: Ben; customer success: Marissa)

Next steps: please review MAP_v1 and the attached spreadsheet answers. If acceptable, we'll schedule a 30-min alignment call on Tue 7/14 to finalize the go/no-go criteria and the test owners.

On the SOC2 items: we can provide a limited evidence bundle (redacted logs, control descriptions) inside the dedicated evaluation tenant — will confirm the list in the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: MAP_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Laura Benton <laura.benton@lighthousehealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Technical acceptance tests and measurement plan

Laura — quick technical note ahead of tomorrow's alignment call. Below are concrete, runnable acceptance checks we recommend including in your test harness (we can provide a pytest-style runner you can run in your environment):

1) Functional concordance suite (scripted):
  - 200 curated prompts with labeled spans; pass = >82% exact span match (we'll provide the JSON-Lines; you can run locally)

2) Latency under load:
  - Synthetic concurrency profile to mirror your peak (40 concurrent sessions) for 512-token responses; metric target: 95th pct < 280ms; test duration: 30 minutes with warm cache and 30 minutes cold start

3) Cost telemetry:
  - Instrument token counts + batch size; compute effective $/1k tokens over the 2-hour steady-state window; we'll provide recommended batching config (batch size 8/16 depending on model)

4) Data protection checks:
  - Inject PHI-like markers in synthetic requests; verify logs show redaction; confirm no PII written to persistent storage (we will share the log sampling script)

5) Fallback/resilience test:
  - Simulate region outage and validate automatic fallback to regional replica within SLA window (expected failover < 30s)

I'll drop the test runner and a sample report template in the shared drive link before the call.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the clarity. A few procurement/security asks so our internal teams can sign off quickly: 
- We will need a small SOC2 evidence bundle (control descriptions + redacted logs) and a statement of how long ephemeral KV cache entries live during evaluation.
- Can you confirm who will have admin access in the evaluation tenant? Our security team requires two named customer-side admins for auditability.
- Proposed decision date of 2026-08-31 is fine but procurement wants a 2-week contingency in case any pass/fail remediations are requested. Can we push the final PO date to 2026-09-14 (conditional on passing acceptance)?

I'll attach our internal questionnaire; expect some fields to be completed by your security team.

— Samir

Subject: Re: Evaluation window + acceptance criteria (MAP kickoff)

Samir — noted and agreed on process. Short answers below and next steps: 

1) SOC2 evidence: we will produce a redacted bundle for your SOC2 checklist items (control descriptions, redacted request/response logs, and a short attestation from our Compliance team). We'll mark items that require NDAs/justified redaction on the bundle.

2) KV cache TTL: default evaluation TTL is 4 hours; we can expose a configuration knob to reduce to 30 minutes for parity testing. We'll document TTL behavior in the runbook.

3) Admin access: we propose two customer-admin seats (Samir + Laura) and two Redwood-side admins (Karthik + Marissa). Admin activity will be auditable and we will provide the audit log extracts as part of the evidence bundle.

4) Timeline: we can accept the conditional PO date of 2026-09-14 as the procurement buffer. Our recommended decision milestone remains 2026-08-31; if remediation work is needed, we'll run a 2-week remediation sprint ending 2026-09-14.

Next action: Ben will send an updated MAP with the admin roster and the conditional timeline. Can we confirm a Tue 7/20 start so test owners have a week to instrument?

Best,
Marissa
